messages:
jon: Quick readout from today's microbench: compared fp16 / int8 / int6 on atlas-7b across 2k eval slices (mix: short chat, structured extraction, longform summarization). Putting a short handoff for GTN/product. Link: https://internal.redwood/bench/3655

maria: Appreciate it. Paste the concise scorecard pls.

jon: Scorecard (2k mixed slices):
```
metric            | fp16 (base) | int8   | int6   | delta (int8/int6 vs fp16)
QA F1             | 0.891       | 0.884  | 0.865  | -0.8% / -2.9%
Exact Match (EM)  | 0.828       | 0.822  | 0.798  | -0.7% / -3.6%
ROUGE-L           | 0.437       | 0.432  | 0.415  | -1.1% / -5.0%
Latency p50 (ms)  | 115         | 128    | 136    | +11% / +18%
Latency p95 (ms)  | 320         | 365    | 410    | +14% / +28%
Cost / 1k tokens  | $0.44       | $0.31  | $0.22  | -30% / -50%
Throughput (req/s) | 8.5        | 9.8    | 10.6   | +15% / +25%
```
Notes: int6 (new quant backend) gives huge unit cost wins but larger quality regressions on multi-step extraction and numeric normalization. int8 sits in a reasonable middle: ~30% cost down, <1% QA F1 drop on average but p95 latency worsens due to KV cache effects on long sequences.

rashid: Which slices failed for int6 specifically? any reproducible failure modes?

jon: int6 failures concentrated in: (1) multi-bullet extraction with unit conversion, (2) long-document coreference (summaries >800 tokens), (3) rare named-entity disambiguation. Short QA/chat and paraphrase detection were fine. Example failure: "List all error codes and map to severity (1-5)." int6 omitted low-frequency codes.

claire: For product routing language, can we give a simple tiered recommendation?

jon: Proposed GTN defaults: Economy (exploratory/self-serve) -> int6; Balanced (default product endpoints) -> int8; Premium (SLA / critical extraction) -> fp16. Also suggest hybrid rules to send extraction-heavy or long requests to Premium.

Sample router policy (drop-in):
```json
{
  "routes": [
    {"name": "premium", "predicate": "tokens>1024 || task==\"extraction\" || confidence<0.65", "model": "atlas-7b-fp16"},
    {"name": "balanced", "predicate": "user_tier==\"default\" && tokens<=1024", "model": "atlas-7b-int8"},
    {"name": "economy", "predicate": "user_tier==\"exploratory\"", "model": "atlas-7b-int6"}
  ]
}
```

maria: Nice. What runtime guardrails do you recommend for safety/quality monitoring?

jon: Guardrails:
- Shadowing: mirror 0.5% of economy/balanced traffic to fp16; compute rolling deltas on QA F1 & EM. Trigger paged alert if delta > 2% sustained over 15m.
- Adversarial hourly probe: run 200 examples covering numeric extraction, unit normalization, longform coref. Fail-fast if EM drops >3%.
- Latency SLO watch: if p95 for int8/int6 exceeds fp16 p95 by >25% and error rate increases, throttle to balanced/premium.
- Implement a small online sketch of token-level hallucination by checking entity density vs source when source present.

bench-bot: canary created: bench/canary-3655-quant -> 2k simulated requests over 2h. Results will auto-post to #eng-ml/bench-reports when complete.

rashid: For GTN handoff blurb: "Recommend tiered defaults: economy=int6 for discovery, balanced=int8 for general product, premium=fp16 for critical extraction/longform. Shadow small percent to detect drift; auto-fallback to premium on sustained quality regressions."

claire: Product wants one-slide numbers: Ill use: "~30% cost reduction with int8 (vs fp16), ~50% with int6; expected average QA F1 drop: int8 ~0.8%, int6 ~3% (workload dependent). Recommend tiered routing + 0.5% shadowing and hourly adversarial checks."

jon: I'll follow up with a short doc and add the router snippet to GTN snippets. Will also attach the full per-slice breakdown after canary.

maria: Great work 44d

jon: thanks — will ping when bench reports land.
